findings.reason: the plan already sequences §9/§11 in f-afl-002's body for exactly this same-file reason, and adding §12 to that record (with its §10 ordering) is the content change that keeps the plan's next-step record and its new section consistent.
findings.text: §12 is an open, implementable section that no followup carries and whose required ordering after §10 is unrecorded in the plan: the only open followup f-afl-002's body names §9, §10 and §11 and its prompt invokes `§9`, while §12 changes `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py` — the same two files §10 changes — so a coordinator working from the plan's own next-step record either never dispatches §12 or dispatches it concurrently with §10 into one file

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/session_host.py:_fifo_path` (line 204) and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:_session_host_fifo` (line 1319) both exist and both compose `f"{pid}-{start}.fifo"`; the cited §9 follow-on is stated in the §9 node comment on the plan; the s8 landed summary now points at `/reckon/evidence/archive/a-follower-lives-as-long-as-its-session-landed.html#s8-session-end`, file and anchor both present; commit anchors `9dfb2a1e`, `750f677a`, `9435a8b9`, `60e7f26b`, `8775e225` resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §12's done-when names the equality test between the host and dispatch resolvers, the grep `{pid}-{start}.fifo` appearing once in `reckon/`, the two test files that must pass, and a negative control (the equality test fails when one side's format is changed alone, which is constructible by re-inlining a side-specific format) — each clause is measurably falsifiable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §12's gates are `tests/test_session_host.py` and `tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py`, both in the repository's own tree and both present; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §12 names modules and functions by what they do; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §12's stated root cause (the FIFO filename format duplicated in two Python readers) matches the cited §9 follow-on and the code (the literal appears at dispatch.py:1326 and session_host.py:226), and the mechanism runs on real callers (`SessionHost.__init__` stores `_fifo_path(...)`; `_ask_session_host_for_follower` writes to `_session_host_fifo()`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §12 carries one deliverable (one Python function names the FIFO, both readers call it); §10 and §11 each carry one.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §12's required build order (after the dry-run node §10, which edits the same `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `tests/test_dispatch_session_host.py`) and §12's own existence are recorded nowhere in the plan: the open followup f-afl-002 enumerates §9/§10/§11 and its prompt invokes §9, and the only statement of the ordering is the commit subject of `21291af4e`.
